groups.title: Section A · 第 1 篇 · 1–4 题
groups.material:
M: Good morning. My name is Bob Fetterman. I'm the computer technician.
W: Didn't I call for you last week?
M: Maybe? I work for Alpha Maintenance. I imagine someone from your office called our central office and I'm the engineer designated to your case.
W: Yeah, I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday, which is now 10 days ago. I made it clear it was an urgent matter and please send someone as soon as possible. Couldn't you or someone else have come sooner?
M: I'm sorry, but I'm not in charge of scheduling all logistics. I simply do not know. All I can tell you is I got the call this week and came as soon as I could.
W: I see. Well, I'll have you know, my manager is rather indignant that it's taken you this long to come. I understand it might not be your fault, but nevertheless, you should know what the feeling is around here.
M: I understand, and I'm sorry for any inconvenience. I will try to resolve your computer problem as swiftly and optimally as I can. What and where is the issue?
W: It's this machine right here. It was running slow for a while, I guess, and gradually got worse and worse. Last Tuesday, it just stopped working altogether. If you switch it on, you will see what I mean.
M: Okay. Do you know if it's backed up?
W: Backed up?
M: I mean, do you know if its contents have been copied and saved somewhere else?
W: I don't know.
M: Well, depending on the ensuing operative scenario, if I need to wipe the system directories clean in order to reconfigure default protocols, then my first intervention should be to intricately retrieve all inventories that I can. Otherwise, all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost.
W: My manager would know. Let me go get him.

groups.title: Section A · 第 2 篇 · 5–8 题
groups.material:
M: Have you given more thought to studying law?
W: I've been thinking about it a lot, yes. In fact, this is why I wished to speak to you. I wanted to hear more about what it's like.
M: A career in law is a beautiful thing in my opinion. Many people will say it's a boring field, but I disagree. The thing is there are many different branches of law and many different jobs.
W: You are involved with buildings and construction, right?
M: Correct. I'm a solicitor, specializing in real estate. Most of my work involves mediating land disputes.
W: Do you mind giving me an example?
M: Sure. So in many cases I am employed to arbitrate between two clashing parties. Let's say for example, there are two landowners who are in a thorny disagreement about something like the borders of their adjacent plots. Someone may employ me to break the deadlock and resolve the dispute. Often my work involves negotiating agreements, plain and simple.
W: So you are saying that a lot of what you do is fix people's legal issues, like you try to find a solution that benefits everyone and that prevents a problem from escalating.
M: Exactly, well put. You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive. For this reason, it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible.
W: I see. So besides knowing the law inside out, you need good people skills, right?
M: Of course. Any job that involves people requires good interpersonal skills, and any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating that argument.
W: Right. So I've been thinking about studying criminal law. I think it sounds very interesting.
M: Mm-hmm, yes. I'd say there's more money in property law, but the stakes are higher in criminal law. I can see how you would find it more interesting.

groups.title: Section B · 第 1 篇 · 9–11 题
groups.material:
When a person tries to access a memory, their brains quickly examine everything stored in it to find the relevant information. But as we age, many of us have difficulty retrieving memories.
In a review published in the journal *Trends in Cognitive Sciences* on February 11th, researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories. While this wealth of prior knowledge can make memory retrieval challenging, the researchers say it has its upsides—this life experience can aid with creativity and decision-making.
Researchers Tarek Amer, Jordana Wynn and Lynn Hasher looked at several behavioral and brain imaging studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it. The studies also showed that when given a cognitive task, older adults rely more heavily on previous knowledge than younger adults do.
While the researchers focus primarily on the difficulties that these disorderly, crowded memories may pose, they also highlight a few situations in which these same memory patterns may be useful. "Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity as a function of enriched memories," the researchers write. They further hypothesize that older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge when it comes to decision-making, where they can pull on their accumulated wisdom.

groups.title: Section B · 第 2 篇 · 12–15 题
groups.material:
There are at least four major problems with work in America today.
First, work can be alienating. Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits made from their work.
Second, workers are not paid the full value of their labor. Real wages have not kept pace with productivity, driving economic inequality and a decline in labor's share of income.
Third, people are time poor. In the U.S., full time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day despite productivity increases. Long working hours contribute to the feeling of "time poverty", which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being.
Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk. Technological innovation could in theory liberate people from the 40-hour work week. But unless changes are made to the structure of work, automation will simply exert downward pressure on wages and further diminish work opportunities.
So, what can be done to alleviate these problems? There are competing visions of the best way to arrive at a solution. One vision is what's known as the "post-work" position. The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time. They assert that although doing some work might be necessary, meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace. Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself.

groups.title: Section C · 第 1 篇 · 16–18 题
groups.material:
Recent studies show that self-control and persistence increase academic outcomes, independence of IQ. Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes. Children who think effort leads to achievement outperform those who believe ability is a fixed trait. Given the link between persistence and academic success, decisions about efforts are particularly important in childhood.
Yet, relatively little research has explored how young children learn what's worth the effort. We all know that infants are keen observers of the social world, but they're not just idly watching; they are tiny learning machines. They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples. Even a 15-month-old infant can outperform a high level computer in such tasks. Could infants also make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort? If so, then maybe persistence isn't simply a character trait. Maybe it's flexible and adaptable based on social context.
To explore this question, we showed 15-month-old babies one of two things—an experimenter working hard to achieve two different goals, or an experimenter who effortlessly reached each goal. Then we introduced the baby to a novel music toy that seemed as if it could be activated by pushing a big button on top. The button could be pressed down, but didn't actually activate anything. Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music. We gave the babies the music toy and left the room. Then analysts who didn't know which condition each baby was in, watched video tapes of the experiment and counted how many times babies tried to activate the toy by pressing the button.
Across one study and a pre-registered duplication, babies who had seen an adult persist and succeed push the button about twice as many times as those who saw an adult effortlessly succeed. In other words, babies learned that effort was valuable after watching just two examples of an adult working hard and succeeding. Part of what's exciting about this finding is that the babies didn't just imitate the adult's actions. Instead, they generalized the value of effort to a novel task. The experimenter never demonstrated pushing a button or trying to make music. Instead, the babies learned from different examples of effortful actions that the new toy probably also required persistence.

groups.title: Section C · 第 2 篇 · 19–21 题
groups.material:
If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more. If you are showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes.
When you have to be somewhere, try to arrive 15 to 30 minutes before you need to. If you always run late, that means you must be failing to account for something you always do. Anticipate that by giving yourself extra time to arrive. Keep track of whether or not you actually do arrive early. You might find that leaving early gets you to places exactly on time.
Set two alarms. Set one alarm that lets you know it's time to drop what you're doing and a second alarm that means you need to walk out the door. Obey the alarms. As soon as the first alarm goes off, stop what you're doing. If it's something you'll be coming back to, like a project for work, make a note to remind yourself where you left off. Grab everything you need and make sure you know how to get where you're going. Aim to be out the door and on your way before the second alarm rings. This will only work if you take the alarms seriously, so make sure you react as soon as you hear them.
Prepare for the day ahead. Have all of your notes and materials organized well in advance of each event, so that all you have to do is grab them and go when it's the actual day. If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before. Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day.
Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings. It soon becomes unbearable to shift between one meeting and another without space in between. If you overschedule yourself, however, you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump. As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events, which can be borrowed from, should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time. Calculate transit time between activities and then add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays.

groups.title: Section C · 第 3 篇 · 22–25 题
groups.material:
Do you think Bostonians put out the welcome mat? Do you find other cities to be more or less polite? Different cities have different feels for visitors. Some are friendly and open; some are formal and distant. Boston tends to seem hurried and sometimes a little rude. That's what some tourists have said. One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities. Take a close look next time you're in Boston, and here are some of the things you'll probably see: people smoking in the subway stations despite the frequent reminders not to do so; pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to do so, ignoring the cars; car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn and occasionally cursing at each other. Drivers who can't be bothered to find a place to park, but instead simply turn on their blinker and stop in the middle of the street.
Sometimes Bostonians seem like they're just too busy to be polite. Why is their city like that? Former U.S. representative Chester Atkins says it's because the Puritan founding fathers were themselves impatient and bad-tempered, and had little time for courtesy. That culture has carried down to the present day, he believes. Boston College professor Thomas O'Connor thinks a contributing factor is Boston's history as a city where each new group of immigrants was treated with suspicion and exclusion. That's given Boston a sense of clannishness and reserve, he thinks. The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says. People will begin a conversation with someone they know, but not with a stranger. Ralph Whitehead, a professor of journalism at the University of Massachusetts at Amherst, thinks it's because Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions. By being snobbish about manners, Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy, he says.
Some say that's just the way Boston is and that the city will never change. Still, other cities with reputations for worse rudeness are trying hard to change their images. Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly. New York City is another. There, the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate. If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well.

questions.prompt: What did the woman do last Tuesday?
options: Met the computer technician.
Told the man about her trouble.
Called the man's company.
Visited Alpha Maintenance.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the woman do last Tuesday? 

 【翻译】 这位女士上周二做了什么? 
 A)  见了电脑技术员。 
 B)  把她的麻烦告诉了这位男士。 
 C)  给这位男士的公司打了电话。 
 D)  拜访了Alpha Maintenance。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Called the man's company. 
 【定位】 P4 I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday, which is now 10 days ago. I made it clear it was an urgent matter and please send someone as soon as possible. 
 我上周二跟你们那边一位女士通过话，到现在已经十天了。我讲得很清楚这是急事，请尽快派人来。 

 【信号】 时间锚 last Tuesday 后的应答 。女士主动说 I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday，这里的 last Tuesday 正对上题干的时间锚，紧跟的动作 spoke to a lady there（there 指上文男士提到的 central office）就是她那天做的事，这就是答案句。 

 【替换】 I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday ↔ Called the man's company 通话沟通改写成打电话给公司 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 选项盗用了对话开头出现的 computer technician 一词，但她见到这位技术员是今天上门这一刻，并非上周二；上周二她做的是打电话，时间对不上，属答非所问。  借用原文：I'm the computer technician 

 B) 张冠李戴 上周二她是给公司打电话，电话那头是 a lady，而男士本人这周才接到任务上门，上周二两人根本没接触，把通话对象说成 the man 是张冠李戴。  借用原文：I spoke to a lady there last Tuesday 

 D) 原词陷阱 选项盗用男士自报的 Alpha Maintenance，但那是他工作的公司名，女士只是打电话过去，并没有亲自上门拜访，visited 这个动作无中生有。  借用原文：I work for Alpha Maintenance

questions.prompt: What does the man say he did when he got the call?
options: Consulted someone in charge.
Came as soon as possible.
Informed the central office at once.
Designated an engineer to the case.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say he did when he got the call? 

 【翻译】 这位男士说他接到电话后做了什么? 
 A)  咨询了负责人。 
 B)  尽快赶来了。 
 C)  立即通知了中心办公室。 
 D)  指派了一名工程师处理此事。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Came as soon as possible. 
 【定位】 P5 I'm sorry, but I'm not in charge of scheduling all logistics. I simply do not know. All I can tell you is I got the call this week and came as soon as I could. 
 抱歉，调度安排不归我管，我确实不清楚。我能告诉你的就是，我这周接到电话，已经尽快赶过来了。 

 【信号】 被问者的直接应答句 All I can tell you is 。女士追问他能不能早点来，男士的应答里 All I can tell you is I got the call this week and came as soon as I could 用 All I can tell you is 把重点框出来，这句他亲口交代自己接电话后的动作，是答案句。 

 【替换】 came as soon as I could ↔ Came as soon as possible 尽我所能快换成尽可能快 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 选项的 in charge 直接盗用原文 I'm not in charge of scheduling all logistics，但原文是否定，他强调调度不归他负责、自己也不清楚，根本没说去请示负责人，正好与原文相反。  借用原文：I'm not in charge of scheduling all logistics 

 C) 张冠李戴 central office 来自男士早先的推测 someone from your office called our central office，那是女方办公室的人打给总部，不是他接电话后做的；把别人的动作安到他头上，是张冠李戴。  借用原文：someone from your office called our central office 

 D) 原词陷阱 designated an engineer 盗用 I'm the engineer designated to your case，那是他猜测自己被指派的过程、动作发出方是公司，不是他本人接电话后所为，属答非所问。  借用原文：I'm the engineer designated to your case

questions.prompt: What is the feeling about the problem around the woman's workplace?
options: Frustration.
Intimidation.
Desperation.
Indignation.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the feeling about the problem around the woman's workplace? 

 【翻译】 这位女士的工作场所周围对这个问题的感受是什么? 
 A)  沮丧。 
 B)  恐惧。 
 C)  绝望。 
 D)  愤慨。 

 【答案】 D （态度观点题） Indignation. 
 【定位】 P6 Well, I'll have you know, my manager is rather indignant that it's taken you this long to come. 
 这么说吧，我得让你知道，我的经理对你们拖这么久才来相当愤慨。 

 【信号】 评价性形容词 indignant 。女士说 my manager is rather indignant that it's taken you this long to come，indignant 是直接的情绪形容词，又被 rather 加重，正是描述工作场所对这件事感受的答案句。 

 【替换】 my manager is rather indignant ↔ Indignation 形容词 indignant 转成名词 Indignation 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Frustration 是常见情绪词的合理猜测，但原文用的明确是 indignant（愤慨），二者程度和指向不同：indignant 是对怠慢的气愤，不是单纯的受挫，原文并未表达 frustration。 
 B) 未提及 Intimidation 指被威胁、被吓住，对话里女方是在抱怨对方来得慢，没有任何被恐吓的内容，与原文情绪不符，属未提及。 
 C) 过度推断 Desperation 表示绝望、走投无路，程度远超原文。女方只是不满拖延、表达气愤，并未到绝望地步，属过度推断。

questions.prompt: What does the woman say her manager would know?
options: Whether the contents have been backed up.
Whether they can find help somewhere else.
Whether all data stored on the hard drive has got lost.
Whether they need to wipe the system directories clean.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the woman say her manager would know? 

 【翻译】 这位女士说她的经理会知道什么? 
 A)  内容是否已备份。 
 B)  他们能否在别处找到帮助。 
 C)  存储在硬盘上的所有数据是否已丢失。 
 D)  他们是否需要清除系统目录。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） Whether the contents have been backed up. 
 【定位】 P9 M: Do you know if it's backed up? ... W: My manager would know. Let me go get him. 
 男：你知道它有没有做备份吗？……女：我的经理会知道，我去把他叫来。 

 【信号】 一问一答的指代承接 。男士先问 Do you know if it's backed up?，他随后解释 it 指 its contents have been copied and saved somewhere else；女士最后说 My manager would know，这句 would know 承接的正是前面备份这个问题，所以经理会知道的就是有没有备份。 

 【替换】 Do you know if it's backed up? ↔ Whether the contents have been backed up if it's backed up 改写成 whether…backed up 

 【排除】 B) 未提及 对话里没有任何关于到别处找帮助的内容，女士只说叫经理来确认备份情况，find help somewhere else 是无中生有，属未提及。 
 C) 原词陷阱 选项盗用男士那句 all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost，但那是他对不备份后果的假设性说明，并不是女士说经理会知道的内容；经理会知道的是有没有备份，不是数据是否已全丢，属答非所问。  借用原文：all data that was stored on its hard drive will be forever lost 

 D) 原词陷阱 wipe the system directories clean 直接取自 if I need to wipe the system directories clean，那是男士对自己后续可能操作的描述，是他要不要做的事，不是女士说经理会知道的内容，属答非所问。  借用原文：if I need to wipe the system directories clean in order to reconfigure default protocols

questions.prompt: What will many people say about a career in law?
options: It's boring.
It's challenging.
It's a beautiful thing.
It's unlike most jobs.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What will many people say about a career in law? 

 【翻译】 许多人会如何评价法律职业? 
 A)  它很无聊。 
 B)  它很有挑战性。 
 C)  它是一件美好的事情。 
 D)  它不同于大多数工作。 

 【答案】 A （态度观点题） It's boring. 
 【定位】 P3 A career in law is a beautiful thing in my opinion. Many people will say it's a boring field, but I disagree. 
 在我看来，从事法律是件美好的事。许多人会说这是个枯燥的领域，但我不同意。 

 【信号】 归属信号 Many people will say 。答案落点不在 a beautiful thing in my opinion，而在 Many people will say it's a boring field 这句——题干问的是 many people，必须抓住 Many people will say 这个明确的归属信号，它后面跟的才是『许多人』的说法。 

 【替换】 a boring field ↔ It's boring. 同义浓缩 

 【排除】 C) 张冠李戴 It's a beautiful thing. 盗用了录音原话 a beautiful thing in my opinion，但那是男士『我个人』的看法，题干问的是 many people 怎么说——把说话人的观点安到『许多人』头上，归属错位。  借用原文：a beautiful thing in my opinion 

 B) 未提及 It's challenging. 听上去合理，但录音里无论是 many people 还是说话人，都没说过从事法律『有挑战性』，属凭常识脑补、原文无据。 
 D) 未提及 It's unlike most jobs. 在录音中找不到对应，男士只说了 many people 觉得 boring、自己觉得 beautiful，从未拿它和『多数工作』作比较。

questions.prompt: What does the man say most of his work involves?
options: Arbitrating between disagreeing solicitors.
Preventing disputes from escalating.
Buying and selling property.
Mediating land disputes.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man say most of his work involves? 

 【翻译】 这位男士说他的大部分工作涉及什么? 
 A)  在意见不一的律师之间进行仲裁。 
 B)  防止争议升级。 
 C)  买卖房产。 
 D)  调解土地纠纷。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Mediating land disputes. 
 【定位】 P5 I'm a solicitor, specializing in real estate. Most of my work involves mediating land disputes. 
 我是一名事务律师，专攻房地产。我的工作大部分涉及调解土地纠纷。 

 【信号】 限定信号 Most of my work 。录音 Most of my work involves mediating land disputes 与题干的 most of his work 用词几乎一致，Most of my work 就是定位信号，它后面跟的动作即答案。 

 【替换】 mediating land disputes ↔ Mediating land disputes. 近乎原词对应 

 【排除】 C) 原词陷阱 Buying and selling property. 蹭了录音 specializing in real estate 的房地产话题，听到『房产』就想选；但男士说的主要工作是 mediating land disputes，不是买卖房产，属答非所问的原词陷阱。  借用原文：specializing in real estate 

 A) 偷换概念 Arbitrating between disagreeing solicitors. 借用了后文 arbitrate between two clashing parties 的 arbitrate，但把对象偷换成 disagreeing solicitors(意见不合的律师)；录音里仲裁的对象是两个地主/当事人，不是律师，对象错位。  借用原文：arbitrate between two clashing parties 

 B) 答非所问 Preventing disputes from escalating. 对应后文 prevents a problem from escalating，但那是女士事后归纳男士工作意义的话，且题干问的是 most of his work 的具体内容；用『防止问题升级』这个意义层面的概括来答『主要做什么』，答非所问。  借用原文：prevents a problem from escalating

questions.prompt: Why does the man say it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible?
options: Courts are intended for fixing major legal disputes.
Courts are getting too bureaucratic to function.
Courts can be frustrating and expensive.
Courts can be frightening and arbitrary.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 Why does the man say it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible? 

 【翻译】 为什么这位男士说在可能的情况下最好在法庭外解决问题? 
 A)  法庭是用来解决重大法律纠纷的。 
 B)  法庭正变得过于官僚化而无法运作。 
 C)  法庭可能令人沮丧且费用高昂。 
 D)  法庭可能令人恐惧且武断。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Courts can be frustrating and expensive. 
 【定位】 P9 You need to remember that courts, like all bureaucracies really, can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive. For this reason, it's usually better to resolve problems outside of court whenever possible. 
 你要记住，法庭和所有官僚机构一样，可能非常混乱、令人沮丧而且昂贵。正因如此，能在庭外解决问题通常更好。 

 【信号】 因果信号 For this reason 。For this reason 是明确的因果连接词，它前面那句 courts...can be very messy, frustrating, and expensive 就是『为什么庭外解决更好』的原因，顺着 For this reason 往前一句即定位到答案。 

 【替换】 frustrating, and expensive ↔ Courts can be frustrating and expensive. 原词提取，去掉多余特征 

 【排除】 D) 偷换概念 Courts can be frightening and arbitrary. 与正确项仅差两个形容词，但录音说的是 frustrating(沮丧)和 expensive(昂贵)，不是 frightening(可怕)和 arbitrary(武断)；这两个词录音根本没念，是替换掉真实形容词的近形陷阱。 
 A) 答非所问 Courts are intended for fixing major legal disputes. 说的是法庭的用途，录音里男士并没有用『法庭是用来解决重大纠纷的』来解释为何庭外更好，方向不符。 
 B) 过度推断 Courts are getting too bureaucratic to function. 蹭了录音 like all bureaucracies 的 bureaucracy，但录音只是把法庭比作官僚机构、说它混乱昂贵，从没说法庭『过于官僚以致无法运转』，属由原词过度推断。  借用原文：like all bureaucracies

questions.prompt: What does the man think is required of any law professional?
options: The ability to make arguments in a unique way.
The skill of preventing conflicts between parties concerned.
The skill of foreseeing any potential stakes in their work.
The ability to express themselves clearly and forcefully.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the man think is required of any law professional? 

 【翻译】 这位男士认为任何法律专业人士需要具备什么? 
 A)  以独特方式进行论证的能力。 
 B)  防止相关各方之间冲突的技能。 
 C)  预见工作中任何潜在利害关系的技能。 
 D)  清晰有力地表达自己的能力。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） The ability to express themselves clearly and forcefully. 
 【定位】 P11 Any job that involves people requires good interpersonal skills, and any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating that argument. 
 任何与人打交道的工作都需要良好的人际交往能力，而任何法律从业者都需要非常善于清楚地表达论点。 

 【信号】 要求信号 needs to be 。题干问 required of any law professional，录音 any law professional needs to be very eloquent at articulating that argument 用 needs to 直接回应，needs to be 就是要求信号，其后描述的能力即答案。 

 【替换】 eloquent at articulating that argument ↔ The ability to express themselves clearly and forcefully. 同义替换 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 The skill of preventing conflicts between parties concerned. 蹭了前文 prevents a problem from escalating 与调解纠纷的整段话题，听上去和这职业最贴；但题干问 any law professional 被要求的能力，录音对此的回答是 eloquent at articulating，不是预防冲突，属答非所问的原词陷阱。  借用原文：prevents a problem from escalating 

 A) 偷换概念 The ability to make arguments in a unique way. 借了录音 articulating that argument 的 argument，但录音只说要 eloquent(善于表达)，从未说要『以独特的方式』论辩，unique 是凭空加上的限定。  借用原文：articulating that argument 

 C) 张冠李戴 The skill of foreseeing any potential stakes in their work. 盗用了结尾 the stakes are higher in criminal law 的 stakes，但那是男士比较两类法律时说的话，与『法律从业者被要求的能力』无关，且录音从没说要『预见潜在利害』。  借用原文：the stakes are higher in criminal law

questions.prompt: What did the researchers do in their review in the journal Trends in Cognitive Sciences?
options: They looked into the relationship between one's prior knowledge and creativity.
They offered novel ways to help older adults to keep their memories from aging.
They proposed an explanation for old people's difficulty in retrieving memories.
They advanced a new model concerning human information storage and retrieval.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did the researchers do in their review in the journal Trends in Cognitive Sciences? 

 【翻译】 研究人员在《认知科学趋势》杂志上的综述中做了什么? 
 A)  他们研究了一个人的先验知识与创造力之间的关系。 
 B)  他们提供了帮助老年人防止记忆力衰退的新方法。 
 C)  他们对老年人提取记忆困难提出了一种解释。 
 D)  他们提出了一个关于人类信息存储和提取的新模型。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They proposed an explanation for old people's difficulty in retrieving memories. 
 【定位】 P2 researchers propose an explanation for why this might be happening: the brains of older adults allocate more space to accumulated knowledge and have more material to navigate when attempting to access memories. 
 研究人员提出了一个解释，说明为什么会发生这种情况：老年人的大脑把更多空间分配给积累的知识，因而在试图提取记忆时要导航的材料更多。 

 【信号】 研究行为动词 propose 。定位信号是描述研究者行为的那个动词 propose an explanation for why this might be happening——题干问 do（做了什么），原文里紧跟 researchers 的那个动作动词 propose 就是答案句标志。 

 【替换】 propose an explanation for why this might be happening ↔ proposed an explanation 近乎同词的动作 
 why this might be happening ↔ old people's difficulty in retrieving memories 指代还原为具体所指 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 项 looked into the relationship between one's prior knowledge and creativity 盗用了原文确实出现过的 prior knowledge 与 creativity（见第四段 enhanced, creativity），但那是后文讲记忆模式的好处时顺带提到的，研究综述本身做的核心动作是 propose an explanation，不是去研究知识与创造力的关系，属听到原词就想选的陷阱。  借用原文：older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge 

 B) 未提及 B 项 offered novel ways to help older adults to keep their memories from aging 借用了 older adults、memories 等话题词，但原文从头到尾只是提出解释、分析现象，没有任何研究者提供新方法去防止记忆衰老的内容，属未提及。 
 D) 偷换概念 D 项 advanced a new model concerning human information storage and retrieval 用 retrieval 这个原文反复出现的词制造熟悉感，但原文研究者做的是 propose an explanation（提出一个解释），不是 advance a new model（提出一个新模型）；一个解释和一个新模型不是同一层级的成果，属偷换概念。  借用原文：propose an explanation for why this might be happening

questions.prompt: What do several behavioral and brain imaging studies show?
options: Young adults rely on memory while older adults keep notes as a reminder.
Older adults often retrieve irrelevant memories along with what they want.
Young adults accumulate knowledge much more quickly than older adults.
Older adults generally perform cognitive tasks much slower than young adults.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do several behavioral and brain imaging studies show? 

 【翻译】 几项行为和脑成像研究显示了什么? 
 A)  年轻人依赖记忆,而老年人做笔记作为提醒。 
 B)  老年人在提取所需记忆时常常同时提取出不相关的记忆。 
 C)  年轻人积累知识的速度比老年人快得多。 
 D)  老年人执行认知任务的速度通常比年轻人慢得多。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Older adults often retrieve irrelevant memories along with what they want. 
 【定位】 P3 studies, which show that older adults have difficulty suppressing information that is no longer relevant and that when searching for a specific memory, they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it. 
 这些研究显示，老年人难以抑制不再相关的信息，并且在搜寻某一具体记忆时，常常连带提取出其他无关的记忆。 

 【信号】 show that 引出研究结论 。信号是 which show that——题干问 studies show，原文里 studies which show that 之后的内容就是答案句，紧跟其后列出的 retrieve other, irrelevant memories 正是落点。 

 【替换】 they often retrieve other, irrelevant memories along with it ↔ Older adults often retrieve irrelevant memories along with what they want 代词还原后近乎同句 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 A 项 Young adults rely on memory while older adults keep notes as a reminder 听着像在讲两类人记忆方式，但原文只说老年人更依赖旧知识，从没说老年人靠记笔记提醒、也没说年轻人靠记忆，属未提及。 
 C) 原词陷阱 C 项 Young adults accumulate knowledge much more quickly than older adults 盗用了原文的 accumulated knowledge（见第二段 accumulated knowledge），但原文讲的是老年人积累的知识多、要导航的材料多，从没比较谁积累得更快，选项凭空加了 much more quickly 的速度比较，属过度推断兼偷换。  借用原文：allocate more space to accumulated knowledge 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 项 Older adults generally perform cognitive tasks much slower than young adults 盗用了原文的 cognitive task（见第三段 when given a cognitive task），但原文只说做认知任务时老年人更依赖旧知识，根本没提速度更慢，选项擅自加了 much slower 的速度论断，属原词陷阱加无中生有。  借用原文：when given a cognitive task, older adults rely more heavily on previous knowledge

questions.prompt: What does evidence suggest regarding older adults?
options: They show preserved, and sometimes enhanced, creativity.
They frequently suffer from disorderly crowded memories.
They can rely on their accumulated wisdom in an emergency.
They may well be served by forgetting their prior knowledge.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does evidence suggest regarding older adults? 

 【翻译】 关于老年人,证据表明了什么? 
 A)  他们表现出保留的、有时甚至增强的创造力。 
 B)  他们经常遭受杂乱拥挤记忆的困扰。 
 C)  他们在紧急情况下可以依靠自己积累的智慧。 
 D)  忘记先验知识可能对他们很有帮助。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They show preserved, and sometimes enhanced, creativity. 
 【定位】 P4 "Evidence suggests that older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity as a function of enriched memories," the researchers write. 
 研究人员写道：证据表明，由于记忆更丰富，老年人的创造力得以保留、有时甚至得到增强。 

 【信号】 Evidence suggests 引出证据结论 。信号是 Evidence suggests that——题干用的就是 evidence suggest，原文这处 Evidence suggests that 之后说的 older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity 即答案句。 

 【替换】 older adults show preserved, and at times enhanced, creativity ↔ They show preserved, and sometimes enhanced, creativity 仅换一个程度词 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 B 项 They frequently suffer from disorderly crowded memories 盗用了原文的 disorderly, crowded memories（见第四段 disorderly, crowded memories），但原文那处是讲这些记忆模式带来的困难，而本题问的是 evidence suggests 那句的正面发现（创造力），方向与问点都不对，属原词陷阱兼答非所问。  借用原文：these disorderly, crowded memories may pose 

 C) 偷换概念 C 项 They can rely on their accumulated wisdom in an emergency 盗用了原文的 accumulated wisdom（见第四段 accumulated wisdom），但原文说的是在 decision-making（决策）时可借助积累的智慧，并非 in an emergency（紧急情况），选项把决策场景偷换成应急场景，属偷换概念。  借用原文：may be well served by their prior knowledge when it comes to decision-making 

 D) 与原文相反 D 项 They may well be served by forgetting their prior knowledge 盗用了原文 may be well served by 与 prior knowledge 的近原句（见第四段 may be well served by their prior knowledge），但原文说老年人是靠旧知识 served，选项却改成靠忘掉旧知识 served，把方向反了，属与原文相反。  借用原文：older adults may be well served by their prior knowledge

questions.prompt: What do we learn about American workers from the passage?
options: They are actually proud of the goods and services they produce.
They are worried about being alienated from the outside world.
They are rarely in control of many things related to their work.
They are longing to share the profits made from their work.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do we learn about American workers from the passage? 

 【翻译】 从文章中我们对美国工人了解到什么? 
 A)  他们实际上为自己生产的商品和服务感到自豪。 
 B)  他们担心与外部世界隔绝。 
 C)  他们很少能掌控与工作相关的许多事情。 
 D)  他们渴望分享工作所创造的利润。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） They are rarely in control of many things related to their work. 
 【定位】 P2 Workers are often not in control of how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits made from their work. 
 工人们往往无法掌控自己如何工作、何时工作、他们生产的产品和服务被如何处置、以及他们劳动所创造的利润被如何使用。 

 【信号】 分点首句"First"后的解释句 。本段以 First, work can be alienating. 起头点出第一个问题，紧接着的这句 Workers are often not in control of 就是对该问题的展开说明，是承载答案的句子。 

 【替换】 Workers are often not in control of ↔ They are rarely in control of many things related to their work often not 改写为 rarely 
 how they work, when they work, what is done with the goods and services they produce, and what is done with the profits ↔ many things related to their work 罗列细节概括为 many things 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 A 借用录音原词 the goods and services they produce 制造熟悉感，但录音说的是工人"无法掌控"产品去向，A 却说工人"为之自豪"，态度与原文相反。  借用原文：what is done with the goods and services they produce 

 B) 原词陷阱 B 盗用录音 work can be alienating 的 alienat- 词根，但录音的"异化"指工人与其劳动/产出相疏离，B 却说成"担心被外部世界孤立"，偷换了概念。  借用原文：First, work can be alienating. 

 D) 原词陷阱 D 借用录音原词 the profits made from their work，但录音说的是工人"无法掌控利润去向"，D 却说工人"渴望分享利润"，是录音根本没提的引申。  借用原文：what is done with the profits made from their work

questions.prompt: What does the passage say long working hours contribute to?
options: The steady decrease in productivity.
The adverse effect on physical health.
The feeling of being time poor.
The rising economic inequality.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the passage say long working hours contribute to? 

 【翻译】 文章认为长时间工作导致了什么? 
 A)  生产率的持续下降。 
 B)  对身体健康的不良影响。 
 C)  时间贫乏的感觉。 
 D)  经济不平等的加剧。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） The feeling of being time poor. 
 【定位】 P4 Long working hours contribute to the feeling of "time poverty", which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being. 
 长时间工作会带来"时间贫乏"的感受，这种感受又会对心理健康产生不良影响。 

 【信号】 因果信号 contribute to 。句中 Long working hours contribute to the feeling of "time poverty" 与题干同词出现，contribute to 这个因果信号直接锁定"长工时→时间贫乏"，是答案句。 

 【替换】 the feeling of "time poverty" ↔ The feeling of being time poor. time poverty 与 time poor 同根改写 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 借录音里出现过的 productivity increases 中的 productivity，但录音说的是"尽管生产率提高"（上升），A 却说"生产率持续下降"，与原文方向相反。  借用原文：full time employees work an average of 8.72 hours per day despite productivity increases 

 B) 偷换概念 B 几乎照搬录音 has an adverse effect on psychological well-being 的 adverse effect，却把 psychological（心理）换成 physical（身体）健康，偷改了范围。  借用原文：which has an adverse effect on psychological well-being 

 D) 张冠李戴 D 的 economic inequality 出自第3段 driving economic inequality，那是"工资跟不上生产率"的后果，并非长工时的后果，被错搬到本题。  借用原文：Real wages have not kept pace with productivity, driving economic inequality

questions.prompt: What does automation do, according to the passage?
options: It alters the structure of work.
It puts jobs and wages at risk.
It liberates people from tedious and laborious work.
It creates new work opportunities in the IT industry.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does automation do, according to the passage? 

 【翻译】 根据文章,自动化产生了什么作用? 
 A)  它改变了工作的结构。 
 B)  它使工作和工资面临风险。 
 C)  它将人们从繁琐和费力的工作中解放出来。 
 D)  它在信息技术行业创造了新的工作机会。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） It puts jobs and wages at risk. 
 【定位】 P5 Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk. 
 第四，自动化使工作岗位和工资面临风险。 

 【信号】 分点首句直接定调 。本段分点句 Fourth, automation puts jobs and wages at risk. 开门见山给 automation 定调，是直接承载答案的主题句。 

 【替换】 automation puts jobs and wages at risk ↔ It puts jobs and wages at risk. 近乎原句对接 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 A 的 alter the structure of work 借用录音 unless changes are made to the structure of work，但那是"除非改变工作结构"的假设条件，并非 automation 本身所做的事。  借用原文：unless changes are made to the structure of work 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 借录音 liberate people from the 40-hour work week 的 liberate，但原文是 Technological innovation could in theory liberate——只是"理论上可能"，并被随后的 But 推翻，并非自动化实际的作为。  借用原文：Technological innovation could in theory liberate people from the 40-hour work week. But unless changes are made 

 D) 未提及 录音只说 automation 会 further diminish work opportunities（进一步减少工作机会），从未说它在IT业创造新岗位，D 属无中生有。

questions.prompt: What do post-work theorists advocate?
options: Finding meaning in work.
Prioritizing life over work.
Improving relationships in the community.
Realizing one's social value in the workplace.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do post-work theorists advocate? 

 【翻译】 后工作理论家倡导什么? 
 A)  在工作中寻找意义。 
 B)  将生活置于工作之上。 
 C)  改善社区中的关系。 
 D)  在工作场所实现个人的社会价值。 

 【答案】 B （态度观点题） Prioritizing life over work. 
 【定位】 P6 The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time. ... Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself. 
 后工作理论家认为，工作不应在我们的生活中占据中心位置，也不应占用我们这么多时间。……因此，生活本身应被视为目的。 

 【信号】 表态动词 believe 与结论 Thus 。The post-work theorists believe that work should not hold a central position in our lives 中的 believe 直接引出主张，段末 Thus, life should be seen as an end in itself. 以 Thus 收束出结论，两处合起来锁定立场。 

 【替换】 work should not hold a central position in our lives or take up so much of our time ↔ Prioritizing life over work. 工作不居中心等于生活优先 
 life should be seen as an end in itself ↔ Prioritizing life over work. 生活本身是目的印证生活优先 

 【排除】 A) 与原文相反 A 借录音 meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace 里的 meaning，但原文明说意义在职场"之外"，A 却说"在工作中找意义"，正话反说。  借用原文：meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace 

 C) 原词陷阱 C 借录音 the communities and relationships 里的 communities/relationships，但原文是说意义"寓于"社区与关系之中，并非主张"去改善社区关系"，把举例性说明当成了主张。  借用原文：meaning, purpose and social value reside in the communities and relationships 

 D) 与原文相反 D 借录音 social value 一词，但原文说社会价值在职场"之外"的社区与关系里实现，D 却说"在职场中实现社会价值"，与原文相反。  借用原文：social value reside in the communities and relationships built and sustained outside of the workplace

questions.prompt: What does the speaker say even our personal beliefs about effort can do?
options: Affect our attitude to novel tasks.
Distinguish us in the social world.
Outweigh IQ in importance.
Impact academic achievements.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker say even our personal beliefs about effort can do? 

 【翻译】 说话者说，即使是我们个人关于努力的信念也能做什么? 
 A)  影响我们对新任务的态度。 
 B)  在社会世界中使我们与众不同。 
 C)  在重要性上超过智商。 
 D)  影响学业成就。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Impact academic achievements. 
 【定位】 P1 Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes. 
 甚至连我们对努力的个人信念，都能影响学业成果。 

 【信号】 题干原词复现 + Even 强调 。录音 Even our personal beliefs about efforts can affect academic outcomes. 几乎照搬了题干的 personal beliefs about effort，又用 Even 加重语气提示"这点尤其值得注意"——题干关键词原样出现加上 Even 的强调，就是答案句的信号。 

 【替换】 affect academic outcomes ↔ Impact academic achievements. 近义词整体替换 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 Affect our attitude to novel tasks. 盗用了录音后文 a novel music toy / a novel task 里的 novel（新的）一词，但那是讲婴儿对"新玩具 / 新任务"，和本题"个人信念能做什么"无关，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：a novel music toy 

 B) 原词陷阱 Distinguish us in the social world. 借了录音 keen observers of the social world 里的 social world，但原文是说"婴儿是社会世界的敏锐观察者"，根本没说个人信念能"在社会中区分我们"，是盗用原词的答非所问。  借用原文：keen observers of the social world 

 C) 偷换概念 Outweigh IQ in importance. 抓住了录音里的 IQ，但原文说自控力与坚持是 independence of IQ（独立于 IQ、与 IQ 无关），并没有说"比 IQ 更重要"，把"无关"偷换成了"更重要"，是与原文不符的偷换。  借用原文：independence of IQ

questions.prompt: How did the researchers turn on the music toy in their experiment?
options: By pressing a hidden button.
By pushing a big button on top.
By pressing two buttons at the same time.
By helping the babies push the right button.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 How did the researchers turn on the music toy in their experiment? 

 【翻译】 研究人员在他们的实验中是如何打开音乐玩具的? 
 A)  通过按下一个隐藏的按钮。 
 B)  通过按下顶部的一个大按钮。 
 C)  通过同时按下两个按钮。 
 D)  通过帮助婴儿按下正确的按钮。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） By pressing a hidden button. 
 【定位】 P3 Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button so that they heard the toy making music. 
 在婴儿看不到的地方，我们用一个隐藏的按钮打开了音乐玩具，好让他们听到玩具发出音乐。 

 【信号】 题干动词 turned on 原样复现 。录音 we turned on the music toy with a hidden button 把题干的 turn on the music toy 原样念出，紧跟 with a hidden button 交代方式——题干动作短语原样出现的那句，就是答案句。 

 【替换】 turned on the music toy with a hidden button ↔ By pressing a hidden button. with a hidden button 概括为 by pressing it 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 By pushing a big button on top. 整句盗自录音 pushing a big button on top，但原文说这个顶上的大按钮"按得下去却其实不启动任何东西"（didn't actually activate anything），它是给婴儿试的假按钮，不是研究者打开玩具的方式，是典型原词陷阱。  借用原文：a big button on top, but didn't actually activate anything 

 C) 未提及 By pressing two buttons at the same time. 里"同时按两个按钮"在录音中完全没有出现——原文只有一个隐藏按钮和一个假的大按钮，没有"两个一起按"的说法，属未提及。 
 D) 与原文相反 By helping the babies push the right button. 与录音相反：原文是研究者 Out of sight of the babies（背着婴儿）自己用隐藏按钮打开，并非"帮婴儿按对按钮"，把"偷偷开"歪曲成"协助婴儿按"，与原文不符。  借用原文：Out of sight of the babies, we turned on the music toy with a hidden button

questions.prompt: What could the infants do in the experiment according to the speaker?
options: Perform difficult tasks successfully just by observing how adults acted.
Make generalizable inferences about persistence from a few examples.
Adapt themselves to different social contexts.
Work hard to interact with experimenters.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What could the infants do in the experiment according to the speaker? 

 【翻译】 根据说话者的说法，婴儿在实验中能做什么? 
 A)  仅通过观察成人的行为就能成功完成困难的任务。 
 B)  从少数例子中对坚持做出可推广的推断。 
 C)  使自己适应不同的社会环境。 
 D)  努力与实验者互动。 

 【答案】 B （细节题） Make generalizable inferences about persistence from a few examples. 
 【定位】 P2 They can generalize such abstract concepts as causal relationships and social roles from just a few examples. Could infants also make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples when it comes to effort? 
 他们能仅凭少数几个例子，就归纳出因果关系、社会角色这类抽象概念。那么，当涉及努力时，婴儿是否也能从少数例子中做出宽泛而可推广的推断呢？ 

 【信号】 选项长句原话复现 generalizable inferences from a few examples 。录音 make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples 几乎照搬了选项 B 的措辞，from just a few examples 又反复强调"只凭少数例子"——选项学术长句在录音原话里成段复现，就是答案信号；第4段 they generalized the value of effort 进一步证实婴儿确实做到了这种推广。 

 【替换】 make broad generalizable inferences from a few examples ↔ Make generalizable inferences about persistence from a few examples. 近乎原词复现 + persistence 同义补足 

 【排除】 A) 过度推断 Perform difficult tasks successfully just by observing how adults acted. 借了录音 keen observers / observing 的"观察"之意，但原文说的是婴儿从观察中"做出推断、推广努力的价值"，并没说他们"光靠看就成功完成难任务"；successfully、just by 把原意夸大了一截，是过度推断。  借用原文：infants are keen observers of the social world 

 C) 偷换概念 Adapt themselves to different social contexts. 盗用录音 based on social context 的 social context，但原文是说"坚持也许是灵活的、随社会情境而变"（指坚持这一特质的性质），不是说"婴儿能让自己适应不同社会情境"，主体和意思都被偷换。  借用原文：it's flexible and adaptable based on social context 

 D) 张冠李戴 Work hard to interact with experimenters. 借了录音里反复出现的 experimenter（实验者）和 effort / work hard 之意，但原文说"努力工作"的是录像里的成人 an adult working hard，婴儿是观察者，录音从没说婴儿"努力去和实验者互动"，是张冠李戴。  借用原文：an adult working hard

questions.prompt: What is the speaker's purpose of giving this talk?
options: Offering advice on overcoming habitual lateness.
Exemplifying various recreational opportunities.
Scrutinizing individuals' defining traits.
Suggesting ways for setting priorities.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What is the speaker's purpose of giving this talk? 

 【翻译】 演讲者发表这次讲话的目的是什么? 
 A)  就克服习惯性迟到提供建议。 
 B)  举例说明各种休闲娱乐机会。 
 C)  审视个人的决定性特征。 
 D)  建议设定优先事项的方法。 

 【答案】 A （目的题） Offering advice on overcoming habitual lateness. 
 【定位】 P1 If chronic lateness has taken over your life and turned into a defining trait of who you are, it's likely that you're losing out on job offers, recreational opportunities, friendships, and more. If you are showing up late to your own life, get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes. 
 如果长期迟到已经占据了你的生活、变成你这个人的一个鲜明特征,那你很可能正在失去工作机会、休闲机会、友谊等等。如果你连自己的人生都总是迟到,那就把自己安排好、把准时放在首位、并解决背后的根本原因。 

 【信号】 篇首点题句 。目的题的答案信号是"开头的总起句":首段先点出"chronic lateness"(长期迟到)的危害,再用祈使句 get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes 给出全篇要教的方向,后面各段(设两个闹钟、前一晚准备、中间留时间)都是这句的展开,故它统领全篇、就是目的所在。 

 【替换】 chronic lateness ↔ habitual lateness 同义词替换 
 get organized, prioritize punctuality, and address any underlying causes ↔ Offering advice on overcoming 详述概括为"给建议" 

 【排除】 B) 原词陷阱 Exemplifying various recreational opportunities. 盗用了首段的原词 recreational:录音里 recreational opportunities 只是迟到会"失去"的东西之一,被一笔带过,讲话根本不是在"举例各种休闲机会",属于把局部细节当主旨。  借用原文：recreational opportunities 

 C) 原词陷阱 Scrutinizing individuals' defining traits. 盗用了首段的 a defining trait of who you are:录音只是说"长期迟到会变成你的一个鲜明特征",并非要去"剖析人的个性特质",方向完全跑偏。  借用原文：a defining trait of who you are 

 D) 偷换概念 Suggesting ways for setting priorities. 借了 prioritize punctuality(把准时放首位)里的"priorit-"做文章:录音只把"优先准时"作为众多建议中的一句,全篇并非教"如何排优先级",以偏概全。  借用原文：prioritize punctuality

questions.prompt: What should you do if mornings are a struggle for you?
options: Make the breakfast simpler.
Take the alarms seriously.
Ready yourself in the early dawn.
Get prepared the night before.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What should you do if mornings are a struggle for you? 

 【翻译】 如果早上对你来说很困难,你应该怎么做? 
 A)  把早餐做得更简单。 
 B)  认真对待闹钟。 
 C)  在清晨做好准备。 
 D)  前一天晚上做好准备。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） Get prepared the night before. 
 【定位】 P4 If mornings are a struggle for you, do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before. Before you go to bed, lay out your clothes and pack your bag for the next day. 
 如果早晨对你来说很吃力,那就尽量在前一晚把自己准备好。睡觉前,把衣服摆好、把第二天的包收拾好。 

 【信号】 条件句原话复现+其后应对 。答案信号是题干条件句在录音里的几乎原话复现:录音 If mornings are a struggle for you 与题干一字不差,紧跟其后的 do as much as you can to ready yourself the night before 就是给出的做法,据"条件句之后即答案"锁定此句。 

 【替换】 ready yourself the night before ↔ Get prepared the night before. 近义短语替换 

 【排除】 A) 未提及 Make the breakfast simpler. 听着像应对"早晨吃力"的合理办法,但录音讲早晨那段只说"前一晚摆衣服、收包",从未提及早餐或把它简化,属凭常识脑补、原文未提。 
 B) 张冠李戴 Take the alarms seriously. 盗用了第三段的 take the alarms seriously:那是"设两个闹钟"那条建议里的话,和本题"早晨吃力怎么办"不是同一条,被错接到这道题上。  借用原文：take the alarms seriously 

 C) 与原文相反 Ready yourself in the early dawn. 把 ready yourself 的时间偷改成"清晨(early dawn)",而录音明说是 ready yourself the night before(前一晚),时间点正好相反,正中第一步预读标出的 C/D 对立陷阱。  借用原文：ready yourself the night before

questions.prompt: According to the speaker, what can we do to combat unexpected delays?
options: Finish the prior task 30 minutes earlier.
Keep ourselves from hitting a bump.
Leave time in between activities.
Try to avoid possible hold-ups.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 According to the speaker, what can we do to combat unexpected delays? 

 【翻译】 根据演讲者所说,我们可以做什么来应对意外延误? 
 A)  提前30分钟完成前一项任务。 
 B)  避免自己遇到障碍。 
 C)  在各项活动之间留出时间。 
 D)  尽量避免可能的耽搁。 

 【答案】 C （细节题） Leave time in between activities. 
 【定位】 P5 Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings. As well as giving you space, this time also acts as a buffer between events, which can be borrowed from, should you be held up in a prior meeting, allowing you to still get to the next one on time. 
 学会在各项任务和会议之间留出时间。这段时间除了给你余地,还在各项活动之间起到缓冲作用——万一前一场会议把你拖住了,可以从这段时间里挪用,让你仍能准时赶到下一场。 

 【信号】 段首主张句+buffer 缓冲解释 。答案信号是第五段段首的核心主张 Learn to leave time in between tasks and meetings,其后用 acts as a buffer(充当缓冲)解释它正好能对付"被前一场拖住"的意外延误,与题干 combat unexpected delays 对上,据此锁定段首这句主张。 

 【替换】 leave time in between tasks and meetings ↔ Leave time in between activities. 上位词概括替换 
 acts as a buffer between events ↔ Leave time in between activities. 缓冲机制印证该做法 

 【排除】 A) 原词陷阱 Finish the prior task 30 minutes earlier. 盗用了末句的数字 add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays 里的"30 minutes":录音是说"为意外延误额外加留 10 到 30 分钟",并不是"把前一项任务提前 30 分钟完成",数字念到了、事却拼错了。  借用原文：add 10 to 30 minutes for unexpected delays 

 B) 与原文相反 Keep ourselves from hitting a bump. 盗用了 you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump 里的"hit a bump":录音是说"一旦把日程排太满,碰到颠簸就会迟到",讲的是过度排期的后果,而非教你"避免碰到颠簸";颠簸是无法避免的,要做的是留缓冲,选项把原意拧反了。  借用原文：you'll arrive late as soon as you hit a bump 

 D) 偷换概念 Try to avoid possible hold-ups. 只是把题干目标"应对意外延误"换个说法重述一遍(avoid hold-ups),并未给出录音真正提出的可操作做法;且录音 should you be held up 把"被拖住"当成会发生、需用缓冲化解的事,而非教你"避免"它,这是空泛复述目标的陷阱。  借用原文：should you be held up

questions.prompt: What do visitors find about the cities they've been to?
options: Their lifestyles vary.
Their traits vary.
They have different customs.
They have different feels.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What do visitors find about the cities they've been to? 

 【翻译】 游客对他们去过的城市有什么发现? 
 A)  它们的生活方式各不相同。 
 B)  它们的特征各不相同。 
 C)  它们有不同的习俗。 
 D)  它们有不同的感觉。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） They have different feels. 
 【定位】 P1 Different cities have different feels for visitors. 
 不同的城市带给游客不同的感受。 

 【信号】 开篇点题句 。这是第一段抛出两个问句后给出的第一句陈述 Different cities have different feels for visitors.，独白常在开头先点主题，它直接对应题干问的"游客的发现"，是答案句。 

 【替换】 different feels for visitors ↔ They have different feels. 近乎原句保留 feels 

 【排除】 A) 偷换概念 Their lifestyles vary. 把"feels"偷换成 lifestyles（生活方式），原文谈的是"感受"不是"生活方式"，属偷换概念。 
 B) 偷换概念 Their traits vary. 用 traits（特征）顶替原文的 feels，原文从未说城市"特征"不同，是换词制造的干扰。 
 C) 未提及 They have different customs. 的 customs（习俗）原文没有出现，属无中生有的替换项。

questions.prompt: What did one study find about Bostonians compared with residents of other U.S. cities?
options: They are not as willing to help strangers.
They are not as patient with one another.
They violate traffic rules more frequently.
They become more easily irritated in public.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What did one study find about Bostonians compared with residents of other U.S. cities? 

 【翻译】 一项研究发现,与美国其他城市的居民相比,Boston人有什么特点? 
 A)  他们不太愿意帮助陌生人。 
 B)  他们彼此之间不太有耐心。 
 C)  他们更频繁地违反交通规则。 
 D)  他们在公共场合更容易被激怒。 

 【答案】 A （细节题） They are not as willing to help strangers. 
 【定位】 P1 One study found that people here are less willing to volunteer to help strangers than those residents of other U.S. cities. 
 一项研究发现，与美国其它城市的居民相比，这里的人更不愿意主动帮助陌生人。 

 【信号】 study found 信号词 。句首 One study found that 是题干 one study 的直接对应锚点，其后跟的就是研究结论，是答案句。 

 【替换】 less willing to volunteer to help strangers ↔ They are not as willing to help strangers. less=not as 同义改写 

 【排除】 B) 答非所问 not as patient with one another 里的 patient 来自后文 too busy to be polite 的语境联想，但研究句说的是"帮陌生人"不是"彼此有无耐心"，把别处内容安到研究结论上，属答非所问。  借用原文：Sometimes Bostonians seem like they're just too busy to be polite. 

 C) 原词陷阱 violate traffic rules more frequently 盗用第一段后半罗列的现象——pedestrians walking when the crosswalk lights say not to、car drivers speeding，但这些是说话人列举的所见，不是 one study 的结论，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：car drivers speeding, making a loud noise with the horn 

 D) 过度推断 more easily irritated in public 由后文 cursing、rude 的氛围引申而来，但研究句并未说波士顿人"更易动怒"，是顺着语气过度推断。  借用原文：occasionally cursing at each other

questions.prompt: What does Thomas O'Connor say about the idea of strangers greeting one another?
options: It was practiced by Boston's founding fathers.
It is not deemed exotic by Proper Bostonians.
It was adopted by Boston's upper class.
It is not part of Boston's local culture.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does Thomas O'Connor say about the idea of strangers greeting one another? 

 【翻译】 Thomas O'Connor对陌生人互相问候这一想法有何看法? 
 A)  这是Boston建城先辈们践行的做法。 
 B)  正统Boston人并不认为这是异域风俗。 
 C)  这被Boston上层阶级所采纳。 
 D)  这不是Boston地方文化的一部分。 

 【答案】 D （细节题） It is not part of Boston's local culture. 
 【定位】 P2 The idea of a stranger greeting another stranger is simply not part of the local culture, he says. 
 他说，陌生人跟陌生人打招呼这种事，根本就不属于本地文化。 

 【信号】 he says 归属信号 。这句以 he says 收尾，he 回指本段正在论述的 Thomas O'Connor，把观点准确归到他名下；其内容直接回答"陌生人打招呼"与文化的关系，是答案句。 

 【替换】 simply not part of the local culture ↔ It is not part of Boston's local culture. near-原句对应 

 【排除】 A) 张冠李戴 practiced by Boston's founding fathers 盗用了 the Puritan founding fathers，但那是 Chester Atkins 的说法、且讲的是性情急躁，与 O'Connor 谈"陌生人打招呼"无关，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：the Puritan founding fathers were themselves impatient and bad-tempered 

 B) 原词陷阱 not deemed exotic by Proper Bostonians 把 Proper Bostonians 这个原词拼到不存在的 exotic 上，Proper Bostonians 出自 Whitehead 谈"以礼仪划阶级"的论述，原文从无"是否异域风"之说，属原词陷阱。  借用原文：Proper Bostonians made other people scornful of courtesy 

 C) 张冠李戴 adopted by Boston's upper class 盗用 Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions，那是 Whitehead 的说法、讲的是上层用礼仪划分阶级，并非 O'Connor 论"陌生人打招呼"，属张冠李戴。  借用原文：Boston's upper class used manners to make class distinctions

questions.prompt: What does the speaker think Boston should do?
options: Stick to its own way of showing courtesy to strangers.
Follow the examples set by Paris and New York City.
Learn from the world's major cities in promoting tourism.
Take pride in its history and adhere to its cultural tradition.
questions.explanation:
【题目】 What does the speaker think Boston should do? 

 【翻译】 说话者认为Boston应该做什么? 
 A)  坚持自己对陌生人表示礼貌的方式。 
 B)  效仿Paris和New York City树立的榜样。 
 C)  学习世界主要城市在推广旅游方面的做法。 
 D)  为其历史感到自豪并坚守其文化传统。 

 【答案】 B （推断题） Follow the examples set by Paris and New York City. 
 【定位】 P3 Paris is one example where people are trying to be friendly. New York City is another. There, the city is trying to persuade subway riders to be more considerate. If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well. 
 巴黎就是一个例子，那里的人在努力变得友善。纽约也是，那座城市正设法说服地铁乘客多为他人着想。如果这些城市都能努力，那么也许波士顿也应该这么做。 

 【信号】 末句 maybe…should 表态 。结尾 If those cities can make the effort, maybe Boston should as well. 用条件句含蓄给出说话人的建议——既然巴黎、纽约都在努力改，波士顿也应仿效，是承载态度的答案句。
